examples.note: Example of a URL containing words from the page title.

rules.quote: Create URLs that contain words from the title of the page with the main keywords close to the start.
rules.specification: The URL slug should reflect the page title and place primary keywords near the start of the path segment.
rules.violation_condition: a URL that does not contain words from the page title, or does not place the main keywords close to the beginning of the URL path
when: The content is published on a webpage with an addressable URL.
rules.why: Instruction on URL construction from page title and keywords.

rules.quote: The URL should be below 100 characters and make sense to the user.
rules.specification: The full URL string must be under 100 characters in length.
rules.violation_condition: a URL that is 100 characters or longer
when: The URL belongs to a webpage.
rules.why: Clear, measurable length constraint on URLs.

examples.note: Example showing hyphens separating words in the URL path.

rules.quote: To separate words in the URL, use hyphens instead of spaces or underscores.
rules.specification: Use hyphens (-) to separate words in URL slugs, never underscores (_) or encoded spaces.
rules.violation_condition: a URL that uses spaces (%20) or underscores (_) instead of hyphens to separate words
when: Formatting multi-word slugs in a URL.
rules.why: Direct formatting instruction for URL word separators.

covers.quote: Titles that are too long will get cut off by search engines.
Write clear page titles. This is the first thing a screen reader user will hear and needs to assure them they are on the right page.

rules.quote:
The title should:
[120752bfa240] LI  include keywords
[55a43c3c1821] LI  be different on each page
[0ce84d05e91d] LI  be 70 characters or fewer.
rules.specification: Webpage titles must be 70 characters or fewer, unique to each page, and contain relevant keywords.
rules.violation_condition: a webpage title that exceeds 70 characters, lacks relevant keywords, or is identical to another page's title
rules.why: G-2: Consolidates title constraints (length, uniqueness, keywords) into one rule.

covers.quote: Describe the content in plain language. This helps users to know if it’s what they need.

rules.quote: Descriptions need to be user-focused and contain keywords. They can be up to 160 characters.
rules.specification: Meta descriptions should be 160 characters or fewer, plain language, user-focused, and contain relevant keywords.
rules.violation_condition: a meta description that exceeds 160 characters or does not contain keywords relevant to the page content
rules.why: G-2: Consolidates character limit and content requirements for meta descriptions.

covers.quote: Write link text that makes the destination and purpose of the link clear.
Ensure the linking text to this page relates to the title.

examples.note: ‘responsive design methods’ used as descriptive anchor text.

parts.quote: Make sure users can read content on all devices using responsive design methods.

rules.quote: Use relevant keywords as the anchor text (for example, don’t use ‘click here’ as link text).
rules.specification: Anchor text must describe the destination or purpose of the link using relevant keywords, not generic phrases like 'click here'.
rules.violation_condition: generic or non-descriptive link text such as 'click here', 'more', 'link', or a bare URL
rules.why: G-2, G-4: Standard rule on descriptive anchor text, absorbing redundant restatements under accessibility requirements.

rules.quote: Link to content on other quality sites towards the end of the content.
rules.specification: External links to other websites should be located towards the end of the page or section rather than early in the text.
rules.violation_condition: links to external websites placed at the beginning or high up in body text rather than towards the end of the content
when: Adding external links to other websites.
rules.why: Specific structural recommendation for external links.
